title: Run the orphaned release-supply-chain forgery harness: tests/integration/release/release-supply-chain.test.mjs executes in no gate
description:
Filed from a worker seat per the standing rail that an evidence row is legitimate when it certifies a capability shipped by a DONE row the filer does not own. That row is task-bf2b2aac (DONE), whose DoD 4 delivered this harness. The defect is NOT in the harness — it is that NOTHING RUNS IT.

MEASURED AT HEAD c3955341, unpiped:

```
vitest.config.ts:32
  include: ["adapters/**/*.test.ts","packages/**/*.test.ts","tests/**/*.test.ts","tools/**/*.test.ts"]
  -> *.test.ts ONLY, so every .mjs misses; also no apps/**

package.json:23 "test:integration": ... && node --test \
     tests/integration/release-supply-chain.test.mjs              <- 1937 lines, 91 tests   LISTED
     tests/integration/release/windows-pack-observation.test.mjs  LISTED
     tests/integration/release/verify-windows-release.test.mjs    LISTED

git ls-files 'tests/integration/**' | grep '\.mjs$'   -> FOUR files, the fourth being
     tests/integration/release/release-supply-chain.test.mjs      <- 146 lines, 1 test   NOT LISTED
```

So the file is not matched by the root vitest include (wrong extension), not in the `node --test` list, and not inside any package so no `--filter` reaches it. **No gate executes it.**

WHAT IT GUARDS, which is why this is filed HIGH rather than as a cleanup. It is task-bf2b2aac's DoD-4 end-to-end forgery harness: it stages a forged pnpm at PNPM_HOME and FIRST ON PATH, copies the repo to a temp directory, invokes the workflow's own pack-step script, and asserts BOTH that the ZIP is absent (or the step exited nonzero with the exact refusal code) AND that `FORGED_PNPM_EXECUTED` appears nowhere in stdout, stderr or the filesystem. Its only recorded executions are HAND-TYPED `node --test <path>` in that row's step-2 comment and its QA record. A supply-chain guard that no gate runs is indistinguishable from one that does, until it is not.

THE MECHANISM, worth keeping because it is not a typo: two files share a BASENAME one path segment apart — `tests/integration/release-supply-chain.test.mjs` and `tests/integration/release/release-supply-chain.test.mjs`. The script names one and the eye reads it as both. The discriminator is never the name; it is enumerating what the runner actually globs against what exists on disk.

RELATED FACT THE FIX MUST NOT BREAK: this repo has THREE disjoint test lanes, and a "repo-wide green" claim needs all three named. (1) `pnpm --filter <pkg> test` — package only, never sees `tests/**`. (2) root `pnpm test` — `tests/**/*.test.ts` etc, NEVER sees `apps/**` (already a global rail). (3) `pnpm test:integration` — adds the `node --test` .mjs half, which neither of the others can reach.

CONSUMER NOTE: no production bytes need to change. The likely shapes are a line in `test:integration`'s `node --test` list, or a rename/glob that the existing runner catches — the choice belongs in the plan, not here.
definitionOfDone: VERIFY-OR-BLOCK first, in a row comment with `git rev-parse HEAD` quoted and greps unpiped with exit codes plus a positive control: the file is still absent from `test:integration`'s node --test list and still unmatched by vitest.config.ts's include; and it still contains the FORGED_PNPM_EXECUTED assertion (if the harness has been deleted or already wired, adopt/verify/report duplicate instead of building).

The harness EXECUTES IN A GATE and the run is proven by its own count line, not by exit code alone: quote `tests N / pass N / fail 0` (or the runner's equivalent) from a standalone unpiped run of whichever lane now owns it. `node --test` prints a count; a lane that prints none has not run it.

A POSITIVE CONTROL proves the new wiring actually reaches the file rather than passing vacuously: plant a deliberate failure in the harness, show the chosen gate goes RED naming that file, restore it, and prove the restore with SHA256 against an out-of-tree backup in a call SEPARATE from the restore (the path is tracked, so `git diff --exit-code` is also valid and both should be quoted).

The sibling basename collision cannot silently recur: either the two files no longer share a basename, or a committed guard enumerates every `tests/integration/**/*.test.mjs` on disk and asserts each is reached by a named lane — set-equality, not subset, so a NEW unlisted .mjs reds rather than being ignored.

The other three .mjs harnesses and both other lanes stay green and unchanged: quote `pnpm test:integration` and root `pnpm test` count lines, disclose foreign red verbatim with path attribution, explicit-pathspec commit.
taskRails: Do NOT weaken the harness to make it pass. If it fails once actually executed, that is a FINDING to report with its output, not a reason to narrow its assertions - it is a supply-chain guard.
No production bytes are required; this is runner wiring. If a fix appears to need a production change, stop and report rather than widening scope.
A gate that prints no count line has not run the file - exit 0 is not evidence. Quote the count.

implementationPlan.description:
RED FIRST (TDD): write the lane-coverage guard, which must FAIL at HEAD because the fourth .mjs is unlisted. Create tests/integration/release/mjs-lane-coverage.test.ts. It runs in BOTH the root lane (vitest.config.ts include `tests/**/*.test.ts`) and the integration lane (`vitest run tests/integration`) - that dual reach is why it goes here and not into lane-smoke.security.ts.

It must:
(1) ENUMERATE FROM DISK, not from git: `readdirSync(join(REPO_ROOT, "tests/integration"), { recursive: true })` filtered to `.test.mjs`, so an UNTRACKED new harness also reds. Make each path relative to the repo root and normalize separators with `replaceAll("\\", "/")` - disk yields backslashes on Windows, package.json holds forward slashes, and getting this wrong makes the two sets disjoint for the wrong reason (lane-smoke.security.ts:58 has a `slashes` helper you can mirror).
(2) PARSE THE LANE from `scripts["test:integration"]` in the root package.json: take the segment after `node --test ` and split on whitespace.
(3) ASSERT BOTH SETS NON-EMPTY FIRST. A parse that silently yields nothing makes the set-equality vacuous and the guard passes forever. Assert `discovered.length > 0` and `listed.length > 0` with messages naming what was parsed.
(4) ASSERT SET EQUALITY, BOTH DIRECTIONS, in one `expect(discovered.sort()).toEqual(listed.sort())` - not a subset check. Every .mjs on disk is reached by the named lane AND every listed path exists on disk. Do NOT add a hard-coded count: set-equality already reds a new unlisted file, and a count would force two edits for one legitimate addition.
(5) Carry a comment naming the mechanism: two files one path segment apart share the basename `release-supply-chain.test.mjs`, the script names one and the eye reads it as both, so the discriminator is enumerating what the runner globs against what is on disk.

Run `pnpm exec vitest run tests/integration/release/mjs-lane-coverage.test.ts` standalone and unpiped. It MUST be RED, and the failure MUST name tests/integration/release/release-supply-chain.test.mjs as the unreached path. Quote the count line and the assertion diff. A red for any other reason (path normalization, bad parse) is a bug in the guard - fix it before moving on.
implementationPlan.note:
RED FIRST, and it reds for exactly the right reason — the diff names the unreached path and nothing else.
```
pnpm exec vitest run tests/integration/release/mjs-lane-coverage.test.ts
  × lists exactly the .test.mjs files that exist on disk
  AssertionError: expected [ …(4) ] to deeply equal [ …(3) ]
  +   "tests/integration/release/release-supply-chain.test.mjs"
  Test Files 1 failed (1) / Tests 1 failed (1)    EXIT 1
```
One extra element, and it is the orphan. Not a normalisation failure and not a parse failure — either of those would have produced a wholesale disjoint diff rather than a single `+` line, which is precisely how I distinguished them.

THE GUARD, and the four properties that keep it from becoming decoration:
1. **Enumerates FROM DISK** via `readdirSync(..., { recursive: true })`, not from git, so an UNTRACKED new harness also reds. A `git ls-files` version would go green on a file someone has written but not yet added — the exact window this row exists to close.
2. **Parses the lane** out of `scripts["test:integration"]`, taking the segment after `node --test ` and keeping only `.test.mjs` tokens. So the guard reads the real runner input rather than a second list that could drift from it.
3. **NON-VACUITY ASSERTED BEFORE the equality.** `discovered.length > 0` and `listed.length > 0`, each with a message dumping what was actually parsed. A readdir that found nothing, or a parse that silently yielded nothing, makes set-equality trivially true and the guard passes forever — this is the failure mode I most wanted to foreclose, since a decorative guard is worse than none.
4. **SET EQUALITY, BOTH DIRECTIONS**, one `toEqual` over sorted arrays. Left-to-right catches a harness no lane runs (this row's defect); right-to-left catches a listed path that no longer exists, which would make `node --test` fail on a stale name. Deliberately NO hard-coded count: set-equality already reds a new unlisted file, and a count would force two edits for one legitimate addition — the coupled-edit trap.

SEPARATOR NORMALISATION on BOTH sides via a `slashes` helper mirroring `lane-smoke.security.ts:58`. Disk yields `\` on Windows, `package.json` holds `/`; normalising only one side would make the sets disjoint for a reason that has nothing to do with coverage, and the guard would red forever while looking correct.

PLACEMENT IS LOAD-BEARING and the file says why: `tests/integration/release/` is reached by BOTH the root lane (`vitest.config.ts` includes `tests/**/*.test.ts`) and the integration lane (`vitest run tests/integration`). `tests/security/lane-smoke.security.ts` would have been the intuitive home, but `tests/security/vitest.config.ts` includes only `**/*.security.ts`, so a guard there runs in neither of the two lanes that matter.

The file also records the mechanism in prose — two files one path segment apart sharing the basename `release-supply-chain.test.mjs` — so the next reader does not rediscover it as a typo.

```
node --test tests/integration/release/release-supply-chain.test.mjs
ℹ tests 1   ℹ pass 0   ℹ fail 1   ℹ skipped 0   duration_ms 29107   EXIT 1
✖ R3-12-F refuses forged pnpm before ZIP production or attacker execution
  release-supply-chain.test.mjs:142  AssertionError
  + actual   '::error title=windows-release::WINDOWS_RELEASE_INPUT_INVALID@WINDOWS_RELEASE_AUTHORITY'
  - expected 'PACK_STEP_FAILED: pnpm provenance invalid'
```
Not `skip` — the platform gate passed, it genuinely executed.

**WHAT FAILED, AND WHY IT IS WORSE THAN A STALE STRING.** Every attacker-execution observable PASSED: no marker file, no `FORGED_PNPM_EXECUTED` in output, no ZIP, `status === 1`. Only the final message equality failed. The expected string is **NOT stale** — it is live production at `tools/packaging/pack-command.ts:193`, `:198`, `:210`. **The harness never reaches it.**

`::error title=windows-release::…@WINDOWS_RELEASE_AUTHORITY` has exactly **one** emitter: `tools/packaging/authenticate-node.ps1:29`. So the run refused inside the Node authenticator's own input gates, two layers upstream of the pnpm provenance check it names.

**GATE ISOLATED** (read-only replica of `authenticate-node.ps1:101-126` against a `git archive HEAD` copy, staged tool-cache, spawned exactly as the harness spawns it):
```
GATE1 Read-ToolchainPins            PASS   schema=moe-toolchain-pins/1 node=v24.16.0
GATE2 RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE/RUNNER_ARCH PASS
GATE3 arch switch                   x64
GATE4 Resolve-SetupNodeExecutable   PASS   (expected == resolved, no reparse)
GATE5 Get-FileHash                  FAIL   "The term 'Get-FileHash' is not recognized as the name of a cmdlet…"
```
`authenticate-node.ps1:109-112` wraps `Get-FileHash` in `try { } catch { Stop-WindowsRelease -Code 'WINDOWS_RELEASE_INPUT_INVALID' }` — so a **cmdlet-resolution failure is restamped as an input-validation refusal**.

**It is parent-process dependent, identical `PSModulePath` on both sides:**
```
powershell.exe 5.1 spawned from pwsh 7   -> GetFileHash=True   (all gates pass, node v24.16.0 launches the entry)
powershell.exe 5.1 spawned from node     -> GetFileHash=False  (INPUT_INVALID)
```
`node --test` is the only way this harness ever runs, so on this host it can never get past the digest step.

**THE VACUITY, which is the actual finding.** I reproduced the same `WINDOWS_RELEASE_INPUT_INVALID` in 4/4 env variants **including two with the forged pnpm entirely absent**. The harness's surviving assertions — no marker, no ZIP, exit 1 — are satisfied by *any* early refusal, exactly the failure its own comment at `:136-138` was written to prevent. `assertForgeryIsReachable` proves the forged `pnpm` wins a PATH lookup; it does not prove the pack ever consults pnpm. **The single assertion that distinguishes "refused because provenance" from "refused because the authenticator could not hash node" is the message equality — and it is the one that is red.** A supply-chain guard that no gate runs turned out to be a guard that does not reach its subject.

Controls: harness byte-identical (`git diff --exit-code` EXIT 0), owned paths clean, index empty, probe workspace under `%TEMP%` removed and absence confirmed. No production or test bytes were edited. Certifies `task-bf2b2aac` (DONE), whose DoD-4 shipped this harness.
